content.text: From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia Timms HillTimms Hill, Wisconsin, July 2014.Highest pointElevation1,951.5 ft (594.8 m)[1]Prominence425 ft (130 m)[2]ListingU.S. state high point 39thCoordinates45°27′03″N 90°11′43″W / 45.450884317°N 90.195397889°W[1]GeographyTimms HillWisconsinLocationPrice County, Wisconsin, USTopo mapUSGS Timms HillClimbingEasiest routeHike Timms Hill or Timm's Hill is the highest natural point in the U.S. state of Wisconsin[3] and is located in north-central Wisconsin in Timms Hill County Park in the Town of Hill in Price County. After being surveyed by Quentin Stevens of Ogema Telephone Co in 1962, Timms Hill was discovered to have an elevation of 1,951.5 ft (595 m). It is less than 1 mile (1.6 km) south of Highway 86, about midway between Ogema and Spirit and about 23 miles (37 km) west of Tomahawk.[4] Timms Hill is located in Timms Hill County Park. A public lookout tower is atop the hill. Visible to the southeast is Rib Mountain (elev. 1,924 ft, 586 m), 44 miles (71 km) away by line of sight.[5] The 10-mile (16 km) Timms Hill Trail connects to the Ice Age Trail,[6] a National Scenic Trail stretching 1,200 miles (1,900 km) across glacial terrain in Wisconsin.The tower at the top of Timms Hill.
